title: Prisoner 8612 (Stanford Prison Experiment, 1971)

youtube.title: You Signed Up for a Fake Prison. You Became Prisoner 8612. #Shorts
youtube.description:
August 1971. $15 a day to live in a fake prison for two weeks. Then a real police car pulls up.

This is the Stanford Prison Experiment, told from the inside as prisoner 8612. It was shut down after six days, and for 50 years it was taught as proof that good people turn cruel. But the archive tapes tell a different story.

What would YOU do when someone in charge tells you to? Tell me in the comments.

Sources:
- Haney, C., Banks, W. C., & Zimbardo, P. G. (1973). Interpersonal dynamics in a simulated prison.
- Le Texier, T. (2019). Debunking the Stanford Prison Experiment. American Psychologist, 74(7).
